## Idea

### Five yap frameworks; three carry 90%
<a id="ideas-takes-epiphanies-story"></a>

Oren's five: strong take, strong take → education, small epiphany ("Do you notice how husbands always do this?"), humour (poke fun at something), story time. Takes, small epiphanies and story time are the foundation of ~90% of content.

> Strong takes, small epiphanies, and story time is like the foundation for 90% of the content you can make.

`idea` · formats: reel60, reel90, yt-short, reel30 · niches: all, travel · stated · from [L06](../sources/L06.md) · ⚠ [C3](../clashes.md#c3)

<a id="ideas-avoid-generic-lists"></a>

### Strong take, then defend or teach
<a id="ideas-strong-take"></a>

### Idea faucets: Reddit and your own winners
<a id="ideas-reddit-faucet"></a>

Sort your niche subreddit by top of the month and have ChatGPT summarise what people discuss; and turn last week's most viral video into one specific buzzword ("creative tax strategies") for next week's video.

> it's a proven conversation starter that's already happening in your niche.

### Copy only true outliers
<a id="ideas-outliers-vs-own-average"></a>

A video is an outlier only against that creator's own average (20K isn't an outlier if they average 100K). Briar keeps a second TikTok account that follows only the niche; Oren's library sorts by ≥2× outliers.

> make sure it's an outlier for them.

<a id="ideas-5-plus-5-creators"></a>

Take topics from 5 niche competitors and packaging (formats, camera angles, series) from 5 creators outside the niche; nobody knows where your combos come from.

> Pull the topics that your niche competitors are talking about.

### You compete with the whole feed
<a id="ideas-compete-with-feed"></a>

Your rivals are everything in the viewer's feed (skits, funny and relatable people), not niche competitors; look outside your niche. Build an account that follows what your ideal viewer follows and check it 10–15 min a day for a couple of weeks.

> I'd highly recommend looking outside your niche.

### Shareability: why would they send it?
<a id="ideas-shareability-test"></a>

The key test is whether someone would send it to someone else (relatable, expertise, tutorial, funny, interesting, beautiful). Our playbook ranks sends per reach as the strongest signal for reaching new people.

> it has to be sharable.

### Green or red, never grey
<a id="ideas-polarise-green-red"></a>

Take a hard stance you actually believe about 90% of the time; keep nuance for private work. People who disagree argue in the comments, which drives reach.

> We don't want to live in the gray.

### Widen the audience one layer higher
<a id="ideas-high-tam-one-layer-up"></a>

For top-of-funnel reach, widen the audience one layer ("college girls that love Pilates" → "ladies"; sales → business → money → ambition) and avoid narrowing words like "business owners", but keep a through-line to what you do.

> most people just need to go one layer higher.

### Content hackathon: make 1–2 wild pieces
<a id="ideas-hackathon"></a>

Monthly or quarterly: a safe-space kickoff, each person makes 1–2 new pieces that will crush or flop (9 a.m.–4 p.m.), presentations explaining why, team votes, the winner runs publicly. Reward innovation, not performance.

> I don't care how anything you make today performs.

### Pause-and-play breakdown of a reel
<a id="l10-pause-and-play-breakdown"></a>

Play another creator's popular or paid reel with its audio in a rounded card. Freeze it at each effect, shrink it to a thumbnail beside your head, explain how to make that effect, then play on. In L10 the source plays 10 times, 19.9 s of 85 s (23%), and its own lines carry the story.

**How:** Card top-right at ~50% width while it plays, ~13% width thumbnail while you talk; whoosh when it grows. Plan freeze times in the storyboard's Freeze column.

> Format: Pause-and-play breakdown

`idea` · formats: reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: all, tech · observed · from [L10](../sources/L10.md) · ⚠ [C31](../clashes.md#c31)
